newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Nov retail sales rise 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Nov retail sales rise 0.9 pct.

text.p: Canadian retail sales rose 0.9 percent in November to a seasonally adjusted C$18.43 billion from a revised C$18.25 billion (C$18.20 billion) in October, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a -0.2 +2.5 C$13.80 bln
Statistics Canada said early indications for December sales pointed to a rise.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.6 percent rise in retail sales in November.

Statistics Canada said sales by retailers of durable goods accounted for most of the overall gain in November. In dollar terms, the largest increases were posted in sales of furniture, which rose 3.5 percent, autos, which gained 2.9 percent and general merchandise, which rose 1.3 percent.
"The cumulative impact of interest rate reductions may have influenced consumers to purchase big-ticket items at low rates of financing," Statistics Canada said.
(For more information from Statistics Canada, contact the Retail Trade Section, Industry Division, Pierre Desjardins at 613-951-9682).
